title: Ahalya is released from her curse, continued
introduction: Rama arrives at Mithila along with Lakshmana led on by Vishvamitra. On hearing that Vishvamitra has arrived at their city Mithila, King Janaka proceeds to him welcomingly. On seeing Rama and Lakshmana near at Vishvamitra, Janaka inquisitively asks Vishvamitra about these two princes. Vishvamitra announces them as the sons of Dasharatha and informs about the adventurous deeds the boys have undertaken.
closing: इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे पंचाशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 50th chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
ततः प्रागुत्तरां गत्वा रामः सौमित्रिणा सह |
विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य यज्ञवाटमुपागमत्
verses.iast:
tataḥ prāk uttarām gatvā rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha |
viśvāmitram puras.hkṛtya yajña vāṭam upāgamat
verses.translation: Rama then travelled along with Lakshmana towards northeast direction keeping Vishvamitra afore and neared the hall of Vedic ritual of Janaka in Mithila kingdom.
notes: The northeast is an auspicious direction, and even today it is held high for any ritual or in the architecture. This direction is presided over by īśāna The God.

verses.devanagari:
रामस्तु मुनिशार्दूलमुवाच सहलक्ष्मणः |
साध्वी यज्ञसमृद्धिर्हि जनकस्य महात्मनः
verses.iast:
rāmaḥ tu muni śārdūlam uvāca saha lakṣmaṇaḥ |
sādhvī yajña samṛddhiḥ hi janakasya mahātmanaḥ
verses.translation: Rama who is with Lakshmana spoke to the tigerly saint Vishvamitra, " the Vedic-ritual of noble-souled Janaka is excellent, indeed with bountifully garnered paraphernalia of the ritual.

glosses.meaning: with, Lakshmana, Rama, on his part

verses.devanagari:
बहूनीह सहस्राणि नानादेशनिवासिनाम् |
ब्राह्मणानां महाभाग वेदाध्ययनशालिनाम्
ऋषि ऋषिवाटाश्च दृश्यन्ते शकटीशतसंकुलाः |
देशो विधीयतां ब्रह्मन् यत्र वत्स्यामहे वयम्
verses.iast:
bahūni iha sahasrāṇi nānā deśa nivāsinām |
brāhmaṇānām mahābhāga veda adhyayana śālinām
ṛṣi vāṭāḥ ca dṛśyante śakaṭī śata saṅkulāḥ |
deśo vidhīyatām brahman yatra vatsyāmahe vayam
verses.translation: "Oh, highly fortunate sage, this place abounds with many thousands of Brahmans who are experts in Vedic practises and who seem to be the dwellers of numerous provinces, and also discernable are the cottages of sages rife with hundreds of carts full with their ceremonial chattels, as such oh, Brahman, a campsite may be decided for us too, as I discern every inch is inhabited." Thus Rama spoke to Vishvamitra.

verses.devanagari:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः |
निवेशमकरोद्देशे विविक्ते सलिलायुते
verses.iast:
rāmasya vacanam śrutvā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ |
niveśam akarot deśe vivikte salila āyute
verses.translation: On hearing the words of Rama that great-saint Vishvamitra arranged a camp at an unfrequented place that has refreshing water.

verses.devanagari:
विश्वामित्रमनुप्राप्तं श्रुत्वा नृपवरस्तदा |
शतानन्दं पुरस्कृत्य पुरोहितमनिन्दितम्
प्रत्युज्जगाम सहसा विनयेन समन्वितः |
verses.iast:
viśvāmitram anuprāptam śrutvā nṛpavaraḥ tadā |
śatānandam puraskṛtya purohitam aninditam
prati ujjagāma sahasā vinayena samanvitaḥ |
verses.translation: On hearing that Vishvamitra has arrived in Mithila, then the best king Janaka instantly forged ahead towards Vishvamitra, keeping his unreprovable priest Shataananda afore of the team, in deference to Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: Vishvamitra's, one chanced [at Mithila,] on hearing
with deference, embodied with [in deference to Vishvamitra]

verses.devanagari:
ऋत्विजोऽपि महात्मानस्त्वर्घ्यमादाय सत्वरम्
विश्वामित्राय धर्मेण ददौ धर्मपुरस्कृतम् |
verses.iast:
ṛtvijo api mahātmānaḥ tu arghyam ādāya sa tvaram
viśvāmitrāya dharmeṇa dadau dharma puraskṛtam |
verses.translation: Even the Ritvik-s, the administrators of that Vedic-ritual, of the great souled king Janaka arrived with post-haste taking holy waters, and they have ritualistically offered that sanctified water to Vishvamitra.

verses.devanagari:
प्रतिगृह्य तु तां पूजां जनकस्य महात्मनः
पप्रच्छ कुशलं राज्ञो यज्ञस्य च निरामयम् |
verses.iast:
pratigṛhya tu tām pūjām janakasya mahātmanaḥ
papraccha kuśalam rājño yajñasya ca nirāmayam |
verses.translation: On receiving that veneration from the great souled Janaka, Vishvamitra asked after the well-being of the king Janaka, as well about the unhindered proceedings of that Vedic-ritual.

glosses.meaning: of Vedic-ritual, without, hindrance [unhindered proceedings,] also

verses.devanagari:
स तांश्चाथ मुनीन् पृष्ट्वा सोपाध्यायपुरोधसः
यथार्हमृषिभिः सर्वैः समागच्छत् प्रहृष्टवत् |
verses.iast:
sa tām ca atha munīn pṛṣṭvā sa upādhyāya purodhasaḥ
yathā arham ṛṣibhiḥ sarvaiḥ samāgacchat prahṛṣṭavat |
verses.translation: Then Vishvamitra asked after the well-being of saints, mentors, clerics, as befitting to their order, and joined the company of all of the sages as a happy-souled sage.

verses.devanagari:
अथ राजा मुनिश्रेष्ठं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत
आसने भगवानास्तां सहैभिर्मुनिसत्तमैः |
verses.iast:
atha rājā muni śreṣṭham kṛta añjaliḥ abhāṣata
āsane bhagavān āstām saha ebhiḥ muni sattamaiḥ |
verses.translation: The king Janaka adjoining his palms then spoke to that eminent-sage Vishvamitra, "oh, reverend sage, please be seated on this high seat, along with these eminent saints in their respective seats." Thus Janaka spoke to Vishvamitra

glosses.meaning: these, saint, eminent ones, along with
in seat, be seated - please be seated on a high seat.

verses.devanagari:
जनकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा निषसाद महामुनिः
पुरोधा ऋत्विजश्चैव राजा च सह मंत्रिभिः |
verses.iast:
janakasya vacaḥ śrutvā niṣasāda mahāmuniḥ
purodhā ṛtvijaḥ caiva rājā ca saha mantribhiḥ |
verses.translation: On hearing the words of Janaka that great-sage Vishvamitra took his seat, and king Janaka also took seat along with his royal priest Shataananda, and the administrators of that Vedic-ritual, namely Ritvik-s, and along with his ministers.

glosses.meaning: [royal] priest Shataananda, administers of Vedic-ritual, Ritvik-s, also thus

verses.devanagari:
आसनेषु यथान्यायमुपविष्टान् समन्ततः
दृष्ट्वा स नृपतिस्तत्र विश्वामित्रमथाब्रवीत् |
verses.iast:
āsaneṣu yathā nyāyam upaviṣṭān samantataḥ
dṛṣṭvā sa nṛpatiḥ tatra viśvāmitram atha abravīt |
verses.translation: On beholding all of them seated all about in their respective seats as demanded by procedure king Janaka then spoke to Vishvamitra.

verses.devanagari:
अद्य यज्ञसमृद्धिर्मे सफला दैवतैः कृता
अद्य यज्ञफलं प्राप्तं भगवद्दर्शनान्मया |
verses.iast:
adya yajña samṛddhiḥ me saphalā daivataiḥ kṛtā
adya yajña phalam prāptam bhagavad darśanāt mayā |
verses.translation: "Today my Vedic ritual is enriched with your advent, whereby I deem that gods have fructified the ritual. Let the ritual be like that. I deem that I have obtained the fruit of the ritual just on seeing godlike you here today.

glosses.meaning: with, fruit - as a fructified one
by gods, effectuated - gods fructified the ritual
by me, fruit [outcome,] of Vedic-ritual, [deemed to have been] obtained.

verses.devanagari:
धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि यस्य मे मुनिपुङ्गव
यज्ञोपसदनं ब्रह्मन् प्राप्तोऽसि मुनिभिः सह |
verses.iast:
dhanyo asmi anugṛhīto asmi yasya me muni puṅgava
yajña upasadanam brahman prāpto asi munibhiḥ saha |
verses.translation: "Oh, Brahman, at which Vedic-ritual hall you have arrived along with so many sages that happens to be mine, whereby, oh, eminent saint, I feel that I am honoured and hallowed.

glosses.meaning: honoured, I am, hallowed, I am.

verses.devanagari:
द्वादशाहं तु ब्रह्मर्षे दीक्षामाहुर्मनीषिणः
ततो भागार्थिनो देवान् द्रष्टुमर्हसि कौशिक |
verses.iast:
dvādaśa aham tu brahmarṣe dīkśām āhuḥ manīṣiṇaḥ
tato bhāga arthino devān draṣṭum ar.hhasi kauśika |
verses.translation: "Oh, Brahma-sage, the scholarly Ritvik-s conducting my Vedic-ritual are saying that only twelve more days are remaining to complete the observation of ritual-pledge, and then oh, Kaushika, it will be apt of you to see the gods who arrive at the conclusion of this Vedic-ritual expecting their due in the ritual." So said king Janaka to Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: then [after those twelve days,] their due, desirers of, gods

verses.devanagari:
इत्युक्त्वा मुनिशार्दूलं प्रहृष्टवदनस्तदा
पुनस्तं परिपप्रच्छ प्रांजलिः प्रयतो नृपः |
verses.iast:
iti uktvā muni śārdūlam prahṛṣṭa vadanaḥ tadā
punaḥ tam paripapraccha prāñjaliḥ prayato nṛpaḥ |
verses.translation: On speaking to that tigerly sage Vishvamitra in this way, the king again asked the sage pointedly and inquisitively with adjoined palms and with a gladdened face.

glosses.meaning: to sage, the tiger, in this way, on saying

verses.devanagari:
इमौ कुमारौ भद्रं ते देवतुल्यपराक्रमौ
गजसिंहगती वीरौ शार्दूलवृषभोपमौ |
पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षौ खड्गतूणीधनुर्धरौ |
अश्विनाविव रूपेण समुपस्थितयौवनौ
यदृच्छयैव गां प्राप्तौ देवलोकादिवामरौ |
कथं पद्भ्यामिह प्राप्तौ किमर्थं कस्य वा मुने
verses.iast:
imau kumārau bhadram te deva tulya parākramau
gaja tulya gatī vīrau śārdūla vṛṣabha upamau |
padma patra viśāla akṣau khaḍga tūṇī dhanur dharau |
aśvinau iva rūpeṇa samupasthita yauvanau
yadṛcchayā eva gām prāptau deva lokāt iva amarau |
katham padbhyām iha prāptau kim artham kasya vā mune
verses.translation: "These two youngsters, oh, sage, let safety betide you, striding like audacious elephants and arrogant lions, bearing a similitude to adventurous tigers and adamantine bulls, and wielding quivers, swords, and bows, are valorous with their valour matching that of Vishnu, and with their eyes broad like lotus-petals and with youthfulness in the offing they look like the exceptionally beautiful twin-gods, Ashwin-brothers, by their physique. How these two have footslogged and chanced here as though immortals have chanced on earth from the abode of gods at their pleasure? What for they have come here, and whose scions are they?
notes: These foots are the same as king Sumati's dialogue at 1-48-2, 3, 4 including anvaya , parsing.

glosses.meaning: with god Vishnu, matching, in valour
[like audacious] elephant, [like arrogant] lion, with strides
by physique, Ashwin, the Twin-god brothers, like

verses.devanagari:
वरायुधधरौ वीरौ कस्य पुत्रौ महामुने |
भूषयन्ताविमं देशं चन्द्रसूर्याविवाम्बरम्
परस्परस्य सदृशौ प्रमाणेङ्गितचेष्टितैः |
काकपक्षधरौ वीरौ श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः
verses.iast:
vara āyudha dharau vīrau kasya putrau mahāmune |
bhūṣayantau imam deśam candra sūryau iva ambaram
parasparasya sadṛśau pramāṇa ingita ceṣṭitaiḥ |
kāka pakṣa dharau vīrau śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, great-saint, whose sons are these two valiant youngsters who are brandishing best weapons? They are embellishing this province as the Sun and Moon doeth the sky. Each to each they are clonal by postural-language, by facial-language and by body language. They appear valorous but boyish in their appearance, as their curls are still jet-black like crow-wings. Thus, whether they are immature by age though mature by their valour or so, I wish to listen about them in actuality.
notes: Import of verses is the same as at 1-48-5, 6, with a little difference in anvaya , parsing.

glosses.meaning: Moon, Sun, [brightening the] sky, as with
by postural [language,] by facial [language,] by body [language]
in actuality to listen, I wish.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा जनकस्य महात्मनः |
न्यवेदयदमेयात्मा पुत्रौ दशरथस्य तौ
verses.iast:
tasya tat vacanam śrutvā janakasya mahātmanaḥ |
nyavedayat ameya ātmā putrau daśarathasya tau
verses.translation: On hearing the words of great-souled Janaka, Vishvamitra whose anima is immeasurable, has announced that those two as the sons of king Dasharatha.

glosses.itrans: mahaatmanaH tasya janakasya tat vacanam shrutvaa
glosses.iast: mahātmanaḥ tasya janakasya tat vacanam śrutvā
glosses.devanagari: महात्मनः तस्य जनकस्य तत् वचनं श्रुत्वा
glosses.meaning: great-souled one, his, of Janaka, that, sentence, on hearing

verses.devanagari:
सिद्धाश्रमनिवासं च राक्षसानां वधं तथा |
तत्रागमनमव्यग्रं विशालायाश्च दर्शनम्
अहल्यादर्शनं चैव गौतमेन समागमम् |
महाधनुषि जिज्ञासां कर्तुमागमनं तथा
एतत्सर्वं महातेजा जनकाय महात्मने |
निवेद्य विररामाथ विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः
verses.iast:
siddha āśrama nivāsam ca rākṣasānām vadham tathā |
tatra āgamanam avyagram viśālāyāḥ ca darśanam
ahalyā darśanam caiva gautamena samāgamam |
mahādhanuṣi jijñāsām kartum āgamanam tathā
etat sarvam mahātejā janakāya mahātmane |
nivedya virarāma atha viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
verses.translation: The highly resplendent great-saint Vishvamitra has informed the high souled Janaka about the coming of Rama and Lakshmana to the Hermitage of Accomplishment, their stopping over there and elimination of demons at that place, their indefatigable travel along with him, beholding City of Vishaala, seeing Ahalya, her reuniting with Sage Gautama, likewise their coming hitherward to gain a grasp of great bow of Shiva. On informing all these incidents to Janaka as well as to Shataananda, who incidentally is the son of Ahalya, sage Vishvamitra paused.

glosses.meaning: indefatigably, to there coming - travelling with him
to know about - to have a grasp of it
